independence.analytical_scope: General replication, no-arbitrage, self-financing, bounded stopping, uniqueness and convexity proofs were checked analytically. Finite test cases verify signs, calculations and implementation rather than proving the theorems.

q=1/2; terminal stock 80/3,160/3,320/3 and call 0,0,137/3. Root call 137/12, shares 137/240 and bank -137/6; up-node value 137/6, shares 137/160 and bank -137/3. Every first-move rebalance and all four terminal paths agree; put 149/12 gives parity -1.

At strike 88, terminal puts 43,13,0 yield down continuation 500/21 versus immediate 28 and up continuation 104/21. Grid 1984/147, European 5248/441 and premium 704/441 agree with independently enumerated policies. The rule uses the observed first branch, not its later completion.

Changing only physical p to 1/4 changes the undiscounted call mean to 43/16 and discounted mean to 1075/441; replication remains 688/49 with identical Q values and holdings. A physical mean-return difference does not create a statewise nonnegative arbitrage.

Payoff dominance gives cE >= max(0,S-K/R^m), and R>=1,K>=0 establish dominance of intrinsic. Backward induction yields equality with grid exercise, allowing ties. R=.98 reverses the strike-financing comparison: 900/49 <20. Enlarged exercise sets cannot lower value only when the underlying market/information are held fixed.

Statewise vertical-spread and convexity inequalities pass through positive valuation. The 70/80/90 butterfly costs -2 and pays 0, S-70, 90-S, 0 on the four stated intervals. Initial receipt alone with nonnegative later cash is sufficient, even if no modeled state falls inside the triangle.

Dated fees and terminal shortfalls match Worked example 5. The least deterministic extra bank reserve for unchanged stock holdings is max(.258,.387)/1.05^2=86/245. Terminal residual is .129 after U and zero after D. The solution correctly limits this optimization to the fixed strategy and fee schedule.

All four report errors are repaired: historical frequencies as prices, future-informed exercise, clipped invalid weights and guaranteed costless hedging despite fees. Criteria require scoped primary reading, quantitative counterexample, explicit trading/dividend/exercise inputs, independent or out-of-sample policy evaluation and separation of consistency, convergence and empirical fit.

Answered explanation includes both cash equations and financed rebalancing. Retention q=1/2, delta=.4, cash=-16 and call=4 are correct; writer surplus 1.5, dividend total-gain entitlement and common-history exercise restrictions are clearly stated.

proof_review.parity_and_bounds: Identical terminal cash plus attainable prepaid stock and matched funding establishes European parity. Positive prices, nonnegative terminal stock and K>=0 justify both upper/lower bounds. American exercise rights are not improperly assigned European parity.
proof_review.completeness: Nonzero S R (u-d) gives unique two-state holdings. d<R<u ensures strictly positive state prices, while either endpoint creates an explicit zero-cost arbitrage if both branches remain possible. Degenerate and zero-support cases are treated separately.
proof_review.self_financing: Inherited wealth exactly buys the next-node portfolio; stock-trade cash plus bank change is zero. Induction covers all paths. History-dependent claims require retaining history instead of assuming stock recombination alone is sufficient.
proof_review.adapted_optimal_stopping: The nodewise choices respect observed information. Bounded finite horizon and conditional iteration prove the stopped supermartingale bound; the displayed maximizing policy attains it. No unproved infinite-horizon optional-stopping result or hindsight policy is used.
proof_review.price_uniqueness: For an overpriced claim, the writer superhedge retains V-C surplus in positive cash and covers any permitted exercise. For an underpriced claim, the holder commits to an optimal stopping rule and shorts its complete-market cash replica. Stopped payments cancel, establishing both price bounds within the stated finite complete market.
proof_review.early_exercise: The call theorem requires nondividend stock, K>=0 and nonnegative funding rates. It is weak dominance with explicit tie cases. The negative-rate and known-dividend counterexamples change exactly those assumptions and preserve their own no-arbitrage pricing equations.
proof_review.scope: No unique incomplete-market price, continuous exercise limit, empirical model adequacy, or universally executable costless hedge is inferred. The fee reserve is not claimed to be an optimal strategy across frictional markets.
